He played [[college basketball]] at [[Baylor University]] and won a national championship. After playing in the [[NBA Summer League]] with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], he decided to pursue a career in the [[National Football League]]. ==Early life== Vital was labeled "middle school basketball's most impressive dunker" by [[Yahoo Sports]] in June 2012.{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Cameron |title=Meet Mark Vital: Middle School basketball's most impressive dunker |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/highschool-prep-rally/meet-mark-vital-middle-school-basketball-most-impressive-151716205.html |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |accessdate=August 6, 2020 |date=June 7, 2012}} He gave up [[American football|football]] to focus on basketball in eighth grade.{{cite web |last1=Werner |first1=John |title=YouTube sensation Vital giving Bears energy boost |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/youtube-sensation-vital-giving-bears-energy-boost/article_00cb25a4-50f7-5d46-b5d9-685c9101b55f.html |website=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |accessdate=August 6, 2020 |date=January 21, 2018}} Vital began high school at [[Washington-Marion Magnet High School]] in [[Lake Charles, Louisiana]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 16.5 points per game and was a Class 4A All-State selection.{{cite web |title=Washington Marion's Mark Vital Named to Max Preps Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.kplctv.com/story/25287969/washington-marions-mark-vital-named-to-max-preps-sophomore-all-american-team/ |website=[[KPLC]] |accessdate=August 6, 2020 |date=April 19, 2014}} For his final two years, Vital transferred to Advanced Preparatory International in [[Dallas|Dallas, Texas]], where he played alongside [[Terrance Ferguson]]. He competed for Southern Elite on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web |last1=Lopez |first1=Andrew |title=Washington-Marion forward Mark Vital more than 'just a dunker' |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/high_schools/article_923ca28e-c6d9-53d1-9537-18a5ca399b53.html |website=[[The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate|The Times-Picayune]] |accessdate=August 6, 2020 |date=July 17, 2013}} Vital committed to play college basketball for [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] after his sophomore year of high school.{{cite web |title=Baylor men's hoops receives pledge from Louisiana sophomore |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/baylor-men-s-hoops-receives-pledge-from-louisiana-sophomore/article_da72a99d-abd4-50f8-83bd-a5f1ebebc4b2.html |website=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |accessdate=August 6, 2020 |date=September 4, 2013}} At the end of his high school career, he was a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and was considered the top player from Louisiana in the 2016 class by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]].{{cite web |last1=Rose |first1=Shanna |title=Big 12 2019-20 Preview: Baylor Bears |url=http://www.bluegoldsports.com/big-12-2019-20-preview-baylor-bears/ |publisher=Blue Gold Sports |accessdate=August 6, 2020 |date=October 30, 2019 |archive-date=September 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200927192448/http://www.bluegoldsports.com/big-12-2019-20-preview-baylor-bears/ |url-status=dead }} ==College career== Vital [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first season at Baylor. While sitting out, he was a member of the [[practice squad]] and developed his offense by playing against [[Johnathan Motley]] and [[Ish Wainright]].{{cite web |last1=Hill |first1=Jerry |title=Vital Not Defined By His Dunks |url=https://baylorbears.com/news/2018/3/8/Vital_Not_Defined_By_His_Dunks.aspx |publisher=Baylor University Athletics |accessdate=August 7, 2020 |date=March 8, 2018}} As a redshirt freshman, Vital averaged 6.7 points and 5.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Werner |first1=John |title=High-flying Vital enjoys doing the dirty work for No. 1 Baylor men |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/high-flying-vital-enjoys-doing-the-dirty-work-for-no-1-baylor-men/article_5b8adca9-08f2-5564-915c-3849a014586e.html |website=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |accessdate=August 7, 2020 |date=February 20, 2020}} On March 23, 2019, he recorded a career-high 17 points and eight rebounds in an 83–71 loss to first-seeded [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] in the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] second round.{{cite web |last1=Watkins |first1=Tim |title=Bears Fall to Gonzaga behind Clarke's 35 |url=https://247sports.com/college/baylor/Article/Baylor-Bears-fall-to-Gonzaga-Bulldogs-83-71-in-second-round-of-NCAA-tournament-130447781/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=August 7, 2020 |date=March 23, 2019}} As a sophomore, Vital averaged 7.2 points, 7.2 rebounds and one steal per game, leading his team in rebounds and steals, and was named to the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Defensive Team and All-Big 12 Honorable Mention.{{cite web |last1=Davis |first1=Seth |title=He's tough, mean and sticky: Baylor's Vital leads the 21st annual All-Glue team |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1646292/2020/03/02/hes-tough-mean-and-sticky-baylors-vital-leads-the-21st-annual-all-glue-team/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=August 7, 2020 |date=March 2, 2020}} On February 8, 2020, Vital scored a junior season-high 19 points in a 78–70 win against [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]].{{cite news |title=No. 1 Baylor 78–70 over Oklahoma State for 20th win in row |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169736 |accessdate=August 7, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 8, 2020}} In his junior season, he helped Baylor become one of the best defensive teams in the nation. He averaged 9.1 points and 6.2 rebounds per game, earning Third-team All-Big 12 and Big 12 All-Defensive Team honors. He was one of four finalists for the [[Naismith Defensive Player of the Year Award]].{{cite web |title=MBB's Vital Named Naismith Defensive POY Finalist |url=https://baylorbears.com/news/2020/3/23/mbbs-vital-named-naismith-defensive-poy-finalist.aspx |publisher=Baylor University Athletics |accessdate=August 7, 2020 |date=March 23, 2020}} As a senior, Vital averaged 12.6 points and 6.7 rebounds per game, helping Baylor capture the national championship.{{cite news |last1=Quillin |first1=Kurtis |title=Baylor's Mark Vital signs with agency founded by Lil' Wayne |url=https://www.kcentv.com/article/sports/baylor-mark-vital-signs-with-lil-wayne-agency/500-b7b572b6-37f2-4196-a994-da95173b3803 |access-date=August 3, 2021 |work=KCEN |date=May 4, 2021}} |first1=Steve |title=Baylor's Mark Vital to Join Blazers for Summer League |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2021/7/30/22601979/trail-blazers-summer-league-roster-forward-mark-vital-baylor-2021-las-vegas |website=Blazer's Edge |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=August 3, 2021 |date=July 30, 2021}} On September 16, 2022, Vital returned to basketball and signed with [[Riesen Ludwigsburg]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]]. He was released on September 23.{{cite web |title=RIESEN-Kaderupdate |url=https://mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de/news/riesen-kaderupdate/ |website=MHP RIESEN Ludwigsburg |access-date=December 14, 2024 |date=September 23, 2022}} In February 2024, Vital signed with the [[Ángeles de la Ciudad de México]] of the [[Circuito de Baloncesto de la Costa del Pacífico]] (CIBACOPA).{{cite news|url=https://www.elnorte.com/aplicacioneslibre/articulo/default.aspx?id=2761195&md5=7f584e0dc9edbe00848a958911ea0f47&ta=0dfdbac11765226904c16cb9ad1b2efe|title=De los Chiefs de Mahomes al basquetbol de la CDMX|first=Rodrigo|last=Goyeneche|work=El Norte|date=February 22, 2024|access-date=February 22, 2024|language=es}} ==Professional football career== ===Seattle Seahawks=== After revealing he was planning on making the transition to football, on September 2, 2021, Vital signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] practice squad as a [[tight end]].{{Cite magazine|last=Coleman|first=Madeline|title=Seahawks Sign NCAA Men's Basketball Champ to Practice City Chiefs=== Vital signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] practice squad on September 13, 2021.{{cite web |title=Former Baylor Bears basketball player signs with the Kansas City Chiefs |url=https://fox4kc.com/sports/chiefs/former-baylor-bears-basketball-player-signs-with-the-kansas-city-chiefs/ |website=Fox4KC.com|date=13 September 2021 }} He signed a reserve/future contract with the Chiefs on February 2, 2022.{{cite web|title=Chiefs sign 13 players to reserve/future contracts|url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/lists/kansas-city-chiefs-practice-squad-13-players-signed-to-reserve-future-contracts/|work=Chiefs Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=February 2, 2022}} He was
